reviews/35/text:
When Timor Leste was occupied by Indonesia, this beach was known as "Pantai pasir putih" in Bahasa Indonesia, or "White sand beach". The name is appropriate - although not particularly imaginative - as the beach is covered in white sand!

When I visited, some 23 years ago, the beach was quite eerie. It was deserted, apart from myself, and there were little concrete picnic shelters dotted along the beach that were slowly filling with drifting sand or become overgrown with trees. There were also some old, decrepit "pedalo" boats, little boats that you can pedal in calm water, that were half-buried in the sand. Clearly, the shelters and pedal-boats dated from the 1970s, some twenty years earlier, when East Timor was a Portuguese colony and a popular destination for Portuguese holiday-makers.

It would be interesting to know if any of the old, decrepit concrete picnic shelters, or any other trace of its old history, still remain.

"Larigutu Viqueque Ossu" refers to locations within the Viqueque Municipality of Timor-Leste, specifically highlighting Larigutu and Ossu, which are administrative areas within the larger Viqueque region.
Here's a breakdown of what the information indicates about these places:
Viqueque Municipality:
* Location: Located in the southeast of Timor-Leste, about 183 km from Dili, the capital. It borders Lautém (east), the Timor Sea (south), Manatuto (west), and Baucau (north).
* Administrative Posts: It comprises five administrative posts: Lacluta, Ossu, Uatu-Lari (also known as Leça or Watulari), Uatu-Carbau (Watucarbau), and Viqueque, which collectively contain 36 villages (sucos).
* History: Viqueque had traditional authority before Portuguese rule. The Portuguese established their office in 1698 and in 1859, Viqueque became a district known as Bibiluto District. It was a district during the Indonesian occupation and became a municipality after independence.

Discover Rai Mutin (White Land), one of Timor-Leste's geological wonders. This unique landscape features expansive areas of exposed white limestone, created by the weathering of the rock's top surface. The result is a striking, foreign environment that contrasts dramatically with the surrounding green hills.

While several areas of 'white land' can be found throughout the Aileu district, this particular site is one of the most prominent and accessible formations. Located just a 15-minute drive from Aileu's main town, Rai Mutin Limestone Park offers a free-to-enter natural experience. It's an ideal spot for photography, a short walk, or simply to appreciate a quieter side of Aileu.
title: Rai Mutin Limestone Park

Disclaimer: My trip was not current.

We stopped by Pousada de Maubisse for a lunch break on our way up to Mount Ramelau or Tatamailau (local language means Grandfather of all) is the highest mountain in Timor Leste and also Timor Island. It is a rest house located in Maubisse, which is the pass over before going to Hato Bulico where we would start our climb. It could be an option for staying overnight if you want to spend more time exploring Maubisse at that time, currently I believe it's under renovation.

It was a tranquil experience for us as no one was around. When we entered the place, there were two rows of rooms on both sides. After that we would pass by a garden with surrounding 360 view before we entered the big house. There was a rustic fire place in the living room, or maybe more suitable to be called dining room. The place was empty and cold when no one was around. The fire place was nice; the whole space was spacious but quite old. We saw a sitting room with two stretch of long sofa, there was a clean toilet with full big bucket of water and a lot of toilet papers.

The food was simple and good, but took very long to prepare. On our way back from the climbing the next day, we ordered before we started the descent and yet we needed to wait for another two hours. I assumed they cooked with fire wood that was why it took much longer but it was good.

It's very nice climb overall and the stopover at Pousada de Maubisse is very memorable. We had the place all for ourselves and it's a nice, quiet, gorgeous, and peaceful time there.

reviews/39/text: Maubisse is full of history to learn and study. 2018 I was filming Timor Awakening 7, Australian War Veteran group was travelling with Ian Hampel, WW2 Commando who was observing Japanese movements 1942 all over Timor-Leste. Amazing story of hardship and survival. I was honoured to spend time with this amazing person. His memories were sharp as knife. Large group of TA7 group was following the paths Ian Hampel walked through Timor-Leste. Postu Maubisse was strategically important spot for Japanese and they stationed lots of troops there. Australian Commandos were observing their movements from the surrounding hills and relayed the information to Australia. Many fights occurred in this area and Commandos disappeared to the mountains with the help of Timorese. Japanese never catched these "White Ghosts".
reviews/40/text: What you pay for is not what you get - mouldy rooms, no hot water, over priced food. What you are paying for are the amazing views. Better to stay at Sarah's guest house and go for coffee to the pousada. Very disappointing!!!

reviews/27/textTranslated:
It's about a 30-minute drive from the center of Ainaro. There's a brown sign on the side of the road. There's a parking space near the sign, and it's about an hour's walk from there. While much of the road is unpaved, there are some stairs and concrete sections, making it easy to walk.
Along the way, you might encounter a man claiming to be maintaining the road who will ask for a toll. He initially asked for $2, but was happy to let me through for just $1 (he was gone when I left).
Just before the waterfall, there's a bamboo bridge. It was installed by an old man who lives near the waterfall (and claims to be the landowner), and the toll is $1.50 per person. You can also walk along the river without the bridge, but the old man will scold you, so I recommend crossing the bamboo bridge.
Because it was the end of the rainy season, we couldn't enter the basin, but the sheer volume of water was impressive.

My friend and I both ordered espresso, but mine was strong and his was weak and watered down. Apparently they made two coffees from the same capsule. This is the type of behavior that made me not wanting to return here. If you are looking for coffee, you can find better alternatives at Timor Plaza, just check out Padaria Brasão, Pau de Canela, or Vista Cafe.
Since this establishment is located inside Timor Plaza, it is not the best place to quietly enjoy your meal or drink. Too much noise coming from inside the mall. Though not big in size, this place is never crowded, which might be an indication of the quality of the food that is being served here (or maybe the restaurant business is going through a rough time). Besides coffee they also have pastries, cakes, and the usual drinks (juices, sodas) available. Prices could be cheaper as it doesn't reflect the quality of the food that you get.
As for Covid-19 restrictions, this establishment does not enforce compulsory hand washing before entering the premises, nor does it enforces or encourage social distancing at the time that I'm writing this review.
All in all, I don't recommend this place. You can find better restaurants/coffee house in Timor Plaza.

Built as a Fort 400 years ago by the Portuguese, the original stone walls, entry archway and cannons are still there. A Magical Stay at Balibo Fort Hotel: A Birthday & Anniversary to Remember

My husband and I recently had the most incredible experience at Balibo Fort Hotel, celebrating both my birthday and our first wedding anniversary. Under the new management of Pelikan Paradise, the hotel has truly elevated its hospitality, making our stay absolutely unforgettable.

The villa prepared for us was stunning, offering a perfect blend of comfort, charm, and a breathtaking atmosphere. One of the most memorable highlights was the romantic candlelight dinner in the garden, beautifully set up with twinkling lights and a cozy bonfire. The ambiance was intimate and magical, making our celebration feel incredibly special.

We had brought our own raw ingredients for a cheese and charcuterie plate, and to our delight, Erin, the incredible manager, offered to prepare it beautifully for us. It was such a thoughtful gesture that added an extra touch of elegance to our evening. The in-house birthday cake was another delightful surprise, not only beautifully presented but also absolutely delicious!

Another highlight of our stay was the immaculate pool—so clean and well-maintained that I didn’t want to get out, even when it started raining! Having the entire pool to myself made for an incredibly serene and relaxing experience.

A special thank you to Manager Erin from Malaysia, who went above and beyond in organizing every detail to perfection. Her warmth, attentiveness, and genuine hospitality made our stay truly unforgettable. We are deeply grateful for the effort she and the entire Balibo Fort Hotel team, now managed by Pelikan Paradise, put into making our celebration so special.

If you’re looking for a place that combines history, beauty, and world-class hospitality, Balibo Fort Hotel is a must-visit. We will cherish these memories forever and can’t wait to return!

Highly Recommended!

With gratitude,
Kivo & Flora

I came to Dili on vacation in good spirits, but ended up having the worst experience ever.

I ordered salmon sushi, bibimbap, jjamppong, sweet and sour pork, one glass of juice, two smoothies, and a Sprite.

However, the juice and smoothies were served only after an hour and a half had passed, and even then, I found ‘plastic’ foreign objects in them multiple times.

I requested an exchange given the questionable hygiene conditions, but they only replaced the smoothies and returned the juice as is, claiming there was no problem with it. I absolutely cannot accept their response of telling me to stir the drinks that already contained foreign objects and drink them again.

The situation became even more serious after that.

The jjamppong finally arrived after two hours, and the sweet and sour pork came out two and a half hours later. However, at that point, they suddenly informed me that the salmon sushi and bibimbap could not be served.

Does it make sense to make me wait for two and a half hours without any notice, only to say now that they can't make them? I seriously doubt their basic operational competence.

The most shocking thing was the owner's attitude.

Given the severity of the situation, I believe the least responsibility should be for him to come out in person, apologize, and explain. However, he hid behind his staff to avoid a response, and when I requested to speak with him, he only repeated that he was "not available."

Yet, in reality, he was inside the store wearing earphones and using his phone. His response was tantamount to deceiving customers.

His hygiene, service, and sense of responsibility are all terrible.

As a fellow Korean, I am truly ashamed. I absolutely do not recommend this place.

ランチにナシレンダンを食べました。入口で注文し2分程で提供。
肉は噛みごたえがあり、しっかりと味がついています。ソースはココナッツの風味がしてレンダンらしさが感じられました。
ご飯の上にかかっているカレーソースは少し辛いですが、それが食欲を増進させてくれます。付け合わせの野菜との相性もよかったです。

reviews/12/textTranslated:
I had nasi rendang for lunch. I ordered at the entrance and it was served in about 2 minutes.
The meat was chewy and well-seasoned. The sauce had a coconut flavor that really captured the rendang flavor.
The curry sauce on top of the rice was a little spicy, but it really whetted my appetite. It also went well with the accompanying vegetables.
At $4, it's a little pricey for a warung, but the flavor was great.
There were a lot of people coming in one after the other during lunch time, so I think it must be a popular restaurant.

reviews/5/responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you, truly, for taking the time to share such a beautiful story with us 🤍

Reading your review felt like reliving that evening through your eyes—from your unplanned late-night visit, to the warmth of the food and the small moments shared at the table. It means more to us than we can fully express.

More than anything, we’re deeply grateful that you didn’t just enjoy the meal, but embraced the experience of Korean food and culture with such openness and joy. That is exactly what we hope to share with every guest—a feeling of comfort, warmth, and connection, even far from home.

Your words about the miso soup, the barbecue, and even the rice truly touched our hearts. These are simple things, but they carry a lot of care and intention from our team, and it means everything to know that it reached you.

Moments like yours remind us why we do what we do.

Thank you for choosing us to be part of your evening—it sounds like it became something special, and we feel honored to have been a small part of that memory.

We will be here, ready to welcome you and your family again, whenever you feel like returning to that feeling ☺️🙏
reviews/5/text:
Our first visit is definitely one for the books. It was one of those unplanned date nights with my husband—after attending a workshop that ended late, we found ourselves hungry at around 9:20 PM. Despite being near the end of their operating hours, the team welcomed us with warm smiles and great hospitality.

We were seated right away with no waiting time, and it was a plus that there’s parking available with a security guard. The menu was promptly given, and within about 10 minutes, our food was already served—sirloin steak with rice, samgyeopsal, beef bulgogi, miso soup, and iced honey lemon (which was incredibly refreshing!).

What made the experience even better was the staff offering to barbecue and slice the meat for us—such a thoughtful touch.

The food itself was truly remarkable. The miso soup tasted authentic and comforting—like a warm hug, perfectly paired with the cool sea breeze. The pork and beef were tender and flavorful, and even the rice stood out—you can tell it’s the kind Koreans use, cooked perfectly.

We finished everything in about 20 minutes—not just because we were hungry, but because the food was genuinely satisfying and comforting. Even my husband, who follows a low-carb diet, really enjoyed the meal (I happily took care of the rice!). And the radish kimchi? Absolutely perfect.

While the price is a bit on the higher side, it’s definitely value for money. Considering the availability of parking, security, authentic Korean ingredients, and overall quality, it’s understandable—especially since many items are imported to achieve that true taste. They clearly don’t skimp on ingredients.

Plus, they also have a Korean supermarket downstairs, which makes the whole experience even better. I’d definitely love to come back with my kids next time and try more items on the menu—I honestly want to try them all.

I’m still daydreaming about all the food we ate until now.

Overall, a memorable experience with great food, excellent service, and a welcoming atmosphere. We’ll definitely be back.

Highly recommended if you’re looking for a place with authentic taste, great portions, and real value – you won’t leave hungry!

ownerDescription:
AHI MATAN represents a source of authenticity and symbolism throughout the Timorese culinary process. "AHI MATAN hanesan simbolu identiku ne'ebe uza iha procesu tein Ai-han iha kotextu Timor nian Timor-nian," Tetum states.

This is remarkable because it highlights the importance of Timorese cuisine and its various complexities (taste, flavors, identity choices, heritage values).

Additionally, we are focusing on educating our palate (Timorese) through the use of heritage legumes, grains, root crops, fruits, and vegetables.
reviews/0/text:
First - Kaimalae Desana/Utasa Gidesa - USD6 - the menu describes this dish as "cassava mix with cassava leaf, papaya flower, baby eggplant, grated coconut, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed for 30mins, served with black bean sauce and pork belly with tamarind sauce".

The mixture looks like Malaysian popiah filling but it tastes so incredibly amazing - earthy and subtle flavor of the grated cassava, cassava leaves, papaya flower. I could eat so so much of this, it's healthy too! Tastes a bit of the daun ubi of the Orang Ulu in Sarawak and the cassava leaves soup of the Rwandans - the kind of food foraged from the forest. 😍😍😍

Topped with a savory, sweet, tangy pork belly stew, something like a Filipino pork adobo. Like seriously damn freaking good with the cassava mix.

I believe if you don't eat pork, you can inform the restaurant to swap for another kind of meat but you really got to try this dish. I haven't been surprised with something I've never had and something so mind-blowingly good in a long time.

Second was the Corn soup (Batar daan) USD5 - I searched the soup but couldn't find the corn? 😂😂 This soup is so heartwarming and nourishing / variety of different beans with some peanut - not salted nor sweet, they serve it with a small plate of salt so you can adjust the saltiness yourself. Served with some tofu, veggies and Tempe. Really good stuff.

The menu prices here are reasonable too and the staff are really friendly. Super super highly highly recommended

reviews/43/text: I was on a quest today to find authentic Timorese cuisine prior to the Portuguese and Indonesian influences. Found this gem, operated by young Timorese entrepreneurs, with a passion for preserving culture and food heritage while also introducing visitors to their cuisine. Ahi matan translates to "the source of the fire." I had such a nice time talking to them, and of course, the food was delicious. I ordered the flatbread made from purple sweet potatoes (which are abundant here), a stew (batar fai) made of grilled corn, red bean, peanuts, moringa leaves, and served with a side of chili-rubbed rosella leaves. The stew was served with a side of tofu and green beans in a rich turmeric sauce and fresh veggie salad with stewed spinach. I washed it all down with a cold glass of soursop ginger juice. I will be returning here again and again.

There is a spacious parking lot and bicycle parking area on the premises.

Mixed experience staying two nights at Baguia Fort. The fort is incredibly atmospheric, and has great views of the surrounding landscape. Our room was in one of the standalone buildings, with two comfortable double beds, and an en-suite (though a few maintenance issues).

The rate was $25 per person for bed and breakfast (egg rolls). Additional meals were reasonable at $5 though of the 5 meals we ate there 4 turned up at least half an hour later than confirmed...

Information on hiking Matebian (the second highest mountain in Timor-Leste) was surprisingly inaccurate, dangerously so, given that is the main attraction in the area.

We drove up to the village of Waiboro, along the worst road I've driven in 2,000km of motorbike riding around Timor-Leste. It was barely passable, and would need a local driver with a decent 4WD or people with good off-road motorbike skills to navigate.

From here it is a relentless 1,100m ascent to the summit of Matebian, with almost no shade. Expect to take 3-5 hours to reach the summit, and another 2-4 hours to descend the way you came. A local guide (helpfully organised by Baguia Fort) is essential as there are large stretches with no clear path.

Starting from Baguia Fort would involve an additional 800m of ascent and descent.

It's an incredible place to visit and stay, but please take into account the information above. Matebian is a rewarding but tough mountain to summit (and drive to reach!).

reviews/7/text:
Forte da Baguia foi um forte Português construído na cidade de Baguia, Baucau,Timor-Leste, durante o governo de José Celestino da Silva (1894 – 1908).

O forte foi construído com um muro de duas camadas, sendo uma externa e a outra interna que o envolve no formato de um retângulo no qual existem três edifícios ao todo. Nos cantos da parede há duas torres e entre elas uma abertura. Envolvendo a parede interna há mais um muro de defesa, que utiliza a encosta como proteção adicional e também uma ponte sobre um fosso na sua frente.

Durante a rebelião de Viqueque, no início de junho de 1959, os insurgentes tentaram tomar o forte.eles contavam com pelo menos cem rebeldes, no entanto, foram repelidos por soldados profissionais, que contavam com um uso mais efetivo dos equipamentos bélicos e também tinham uma metralhadora como aliada. Esta tentativa fracassada de tomar o forte resultou em destruição de grande parte do forte.

O forte foi reinaugurado em 2014, na sua cerimonia de reinauguração contou com a presença de políticos e cidadãos ilustres dentre eles Manuel Gonçalves de Jesus (Embaixador português) Dra. Maria Isabel de Jesus Ximenes (Ministra do turismo) e Dr. António Guterres (Presidente do Município de Baucau), Atualmente o forte funcionam como um albergue.
reviews/7/textTranslated:
Baguia Fort was a Portuguese fort built in the city of Baguia, Baucau, East Timor, during the government of José Celestino da Silva (1894–1908).

The fort was built with a two-layered wall, an outer and an inner layer, enclosing it in a rectangular shape containing three buildings. At the corners of the wall are two towers with an opening between them. Surrounding the inner wall is another defensive wall, which uses the hillside for additional protection, and also a bridge over a moat in front of it.

During the Viqueque rebellion in early June 1959, insurgents attempted to seize the fort. They numbered at least one hundred rebels; however, they were repelled by professional soldiers who had more effective use of military equipment and also a machine gun. This failed attempt to take the fort resulted in the destruction of a large part of it.

The fort was reopened in 2014, and the reopening ceremony was attended by politicians and distinguished citizens, including Manuel Gonçalves de Jesus (Portuguese Ambassador), Dr. Maria Isabel de Jesus Ximenes (Minister of Tourism), and Dr. António Guterres (Mayor of Baucau). Currently, the fort functions as a hostel.

Foodie Critique: Joyful Restaurant (Timor Plaza)

Stopped by this Hong Kong–style restaurant around noon. With only two guests in the dining room—including myself—I expected at least a smile or a welcome. Instead, there was silence and stares. Even getting a menu required me to ask, which set the tone for the meal.

I had come looking forward to a proper Hong Kong–style milk tea, but surprisingly it wasn’t available. Only bubble tea was offered, which I declined. For a restaurant positioned as HK-style, not having this basic staple is a gap.

I ordered the Bitter Melon Beef Rice. Unfortunately, the beef was overly salty, and the bitter melon lacked balance. The only part I can compliment was the plain white rice, which at least helped tone down the saltiness of the dish.

Reflections:
•	When the restaurant is quiet, acknowledging and welcoming every guest is essential.
•	Service should be proactive, not reactive.
•	Food quality needs to reflect the promise of the cuisine—staples should be executed well, and flavors balanced.

There’s potential, but at present, the experience doesn’t live up to the concept. With stronger focus on service and more care in food execution, Joyful could move closer to delivering the true Hong Kong café experience. I wish the team well and hope they can elevate both hospitality and quality.

Nunca tinha estado num restaurante que me exigisse pagar em grupo e me indicasse que não recebia o valor a título individual por não querer ter trabalho. Simultaneamente, apresenta preços na fatura que não correspondem ao menu. Quando pedido esclarecimento ao dono relativamente a esta situação, o tratamento é mais do que arrogante , o que transmitiu desonestidade.
A comida estava boa mas não compensa em termos de preço - qualidade. É exorbitante!
Não repetirei e não recomendo.

The food was good but it doesn't compensate in terms of price - quality. It's exorbitant!
I will not return and I do not recommend it.

ownerDescription: Timor Plaza is more than a retail centre; it is a lifestyle centre where everything for the home and family is available in an attractive, inviting and convenient shopping environment, with easy access and parking. The Timor Plaza Centre Court has also become a renowned arena for social, cultural and commercial activity. It is now the intention of Dili Development Lda. to create five more buildings to accommodate a balanced range of retail, accommodation, office and tourism facilities, constituting a vibrant commercial community that will drive private sector development in the capital for years to come.

reviews/1/text:
Walking into Timor Plaza today, I see a modern building with glass elevators and bright lights. It feels like any shopping mall you would find in other Asian cities. But this place carries a heavy story. It opened in October 2011 as the first modern shopping center in Timor-Leste. It was built by the Jape Group, a family business started by Jape Kong Su, a man born in Balibo who fled the country in 1975 and built his fortune in Darwin, Australia. He returned in 1999 to help rebuild his homeland, and this mall became his biggest project.

Today, the place is busy. The Jape family says more than 3,000 people work in the Dili Central compound every day, directly or indirectly. The mall has a supermarket, banks, phone companies, restaurants, and the only cinema in the country. There is even a free medical clinic run by the Order of Malta. For many Timorese, it is a place to find work, buy goods, or watch a movie. For others, it is a symbol that their country is moving forward.

The founder passed away in 2022, but the Jape family still owns and runs the mall. They plan to expand the compound to more buildings, making it a bigger commercial center for Dili. The mall is a place of progress and business. It is also a place that reminds me of the struggles that came with building it. Both things are true at the same time.

I have to say, Timor Plaza Hotel was such a pleasant surprise! I honestly wasn’t expecting it to be as nice as it was and was really impressed. The rooms are spacious, the beds are super comfortable and the staff are incredibly friendly and welcoming.

The Sky Bar was definitely a highlight. We had dinner there — BBQ meats, salad and fries — and the food was amazing. There was a live band playing, a great atmosphere and the place was packed. The outdoor area, with all the lights and trees, was beautiful, and the views over Dili were absolutely amazing.

We had such a great stay here and I would highly recommend Timor Plaza Hotel if you’re staying in Dili!

This is a place where I could enjoy a refreshing cup of coffee and go shopping when I visited East Timor.

It is a complex facility equipped with various functions, including a bus terminal and a hotel.

I arrived here around 6 PM after coming by bus from Kupang, Indonesia.

On Sunday, I attended church in the morning, and after lunch, I came to Timor Plaza here to enjoy a delicious cup of coffee.

Oh, by the way, East Timor uses the US dollar.

After finishing my entire itinerary, I also took the bus back to Kupang, Indonesia, from behind Timor Plaza.

The time was 6:30 AM.

Anyway, in Timor, I experienced various things here, such as shopping, coffee breaks, and taking the bus.

It is clean and nice.

I passed by here while jogging in the morning, and sometimes runners run in this area. The beach is just a short walk away.

Good. Good.

I recommend it.
